definition: How quantities move over the course of training rather than where they end, and across 6 sources the view that repeatedly separates effects a final-checkpoint table conflates. The archive's instances: entropy consumption and performance gain are both front-loaded, with 73 and 76 percent in the first 200 of 2,400 steps; pass@1 and large-k coverage move in opposite directions across the same steps, and in one distillation study the large-k degradation appears by around step 80 and fluctuates while the small-k gain accrues stably; the exact-tie rate rises across epochs as the reward saturates; and per-task reward trajectories across 20 epochs sort into six profiles including forgetting and stubbornly-unlearned, which a final-accuracy number cannot show. One theoretical source in the corpus proves a training-dynamics result rather than measuring one, on how a transformer comes to learn a chain-of-thought procedure with length generalisation. The operative point for reading the archive is that a method compared at a fixed step count and a method compared at its best checkpoint are answering different questions, and that a degradation appearing before convergence is evidence about the objective rather than about overtraining.

evidence.note: Separates how well a policy currently does on a task from how positively that task responds to further training, shows the second is reproducible across independent runs and predicts downstream value at matched current pass rate, and estimates it from a short probe run before RL begins.
evidence.title: Beyond Solvability: Task Learnability as a Static Prior for LLM RL Post-Training

evidence.note: A survey organizing mechanistic findings about reasoning models into training dynamics, reasoning mechanisms and unintended behaviours, and arguing the field needs a unified theoretical framework.
evidence.title: Towards a Mechanistic Understanding of Large Reasoning Models: A Survey of Training, Inference, and Failures

evidence.note: Confirms that prolonged RLVR makes models forget foundational skills, and counters it with experience replay whose objective weights adapt online to convergence and instability signals.
evidence.title: Beyond Reasoning Gains: Mitigating General-Capability Forgetting in Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Reduces the question of whether an update raises or lowers entropy to the sign of one scalar per token, shows that under GRPO what matters is that scalar's deviation from a policy-weighted baseline rather than its own value, and proves the deviation averages to zero over a batch.
evidence.title: On the Entropy Dynamics in Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

evidence.note: Shows that base models win pass@K on mathematics by producing wrong chains that land on right answers, and that scoring the chain too — CoT-Pass@K — reverses the verdict in RLVR's favour at every K.
evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs

evidence.note: Gives the first optimization guarantee that gradient descent trains constant-depth transformers to solve NC1-complete problems with chain of thought, and shows the algebraic structure of the task decides how far the learned reasoning extrapolates.
evidence.title: Transformers Provably Learn Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Length Generalization

name: training dynamics
